tests.notes: Acceptance evidence: (1) The committed manifest is JSON-Schema valid with capture epic-sandbox-20260922T070125Z-0dac7d6b, capturedAt 2026-09-22T07:01:25Z, approved reviewed distribution metadata, four GET-only redacted requests, and exactly 20 checksum-referenced raw resources: Patient 1, Appointment 13, MedicationRequest 1, laboratory Observation 5. All resource hashes and the exact directory inventory passed the production validator; a separately copied and altered Patient payload was rejected specifically for checksum mismatch. A first negative-test copy used sed -i.bak, and the validator correctly rejected the extra backup file as an inventory mismatch before checksums; rerunning without the backup artifact produced the intended checksum-mismatch rejection. (2-3) New independent adapter assertions compare Patient identity/demographics, medication status/text/instruction/authored date, all lab names/values/units/effective and issued dates, and every appointment status/service/start/end directly against the committed raw JSON. Camila Maria Lopez and Patient/erXuFYUfucBZaryVksYEcMg3 match the source, while mFOLFOX6, Cycle 4 of 12, and the scenario appointment remain absent from EpicClinicalContext and visibly scenario-labeled elsewhere. Explicit absent-field and empty medication/lab/appointment states render 'Not present in captured record'. (4,7) The production-browser Epic path survived reload with the same immutable 2026-09-22T07:01:25Z timestamp and recorded zero requests to fhir.epic.com; missing files, unsupported mode, resource-reference mismatch, malformed capture, and the build-time checksum mismatch all fail closed without an Epic-labeled substitute. (5-6) Backend capture tests prove exact Sandbox-host HTTPS GET-only reads, patient-scoped allowlisted searches, laboratory filtering, redacted evidence, token-from-environment handling, token exclusion, same-origin pagination, ceilings, and fail-closed behavior. Capture-only secret-pattern scanning was clean; no access/refresh token, authorization material, client secret, or private key marker was present. Browser publication is explicitly the reviewed Sandbox test-data package, not UI authorization or a production record. (8) New view assertions confirm capture ID, Patient ID, source identity, and medication are absent from landing, patient, caregiver, and system/graph presentation. The Transportation gateway intentionally enters the existing staff logistics case (as its visible copy states), not a distinct third-party transportation projection; the caregiver projection remains logistics-only. Source-drawer component/E2E evidence verifies dialog semantics, keyboard tab activation, initial focus, Escape close/focus return, original capture time, FHIR/source environment, GET-only evidence, resource IDs, hashes, and displayed-field provenance. Results: backend focused 29 passed; backend fast regression 70 passed with 4 integration tests intentionally deselected by the marker split; focused Epic Vitest 12 passed; complete Vitest 44 passed across 10 files; production build passed; final Chromium suite 8 passed. No executed test was skipped or flaky. Backend emitted two existing dependency deprecation warnings, Vitest emitted existing asynchronous FoundationStatus act warnings, and Playwright emitted the existing NO_COLOR/FORCE_COLOR warning. During tester test development, the new independent suite initially failed 2/3 and then 1/3 on tester expectation/navigation mistakes; only test code was corrected and the final focused/full results above are green. An initial npm-prefix Playwright invocation from the repository root reported no configured project; the exact command was rerun from frontend and passed. The requested .agents/skills/testing/SKILL.md is absent, so testing followed AGENTS.md and docs/standards/TESTING.md.
